evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Not asked. Rep moved directly into probing after customer said 'No' to top-of-mind concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns raised by customer that required follow-up.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided: '$200 hourly rate...includes two movers, truck, taxes, insurance...minimum of two and a half hours...estimate range of around $500 and then we just like to do a range so $5 to 600'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asked: 'Did you want to at least get the truck reserved?' Customer answered 'Yeah, yes.' Booking proceeded without an out.

top_strength: Chauntelle systematically gathered all logistics details (property type, square footage, special items, plants, access, box count, parking) with follow-up questions that clarified the customer's specific needs, building toward an accurate estimate.
coaching_note: Section 1 is missing the quid pro quo framing entirely—jump straight into probing after the customer's 'no' to concerns, without the time-boxed promise and wait for a yes; add the recognizable 'takes about 10 to 15 minutes and you can walk away with a quote you can depend on' line and pause for confirmation before moving forward.
